content.value: Use an indexed loop when you need a position or must replace primitive elements. An enhanced for loop gives each value in order and is useful for read-only aggregation. Its loop variable receives a copy of an element; for reference elements, that copy can still refer to the same object.

The output is 4, 8, 12. Replacing values[i] changes the array. In contrast, value *= 2 inside an enhanced for loop would change only the local primitive variable. Use i < values.length to avoid an invalid index.
Practice: trace the example by hand, change one input, and explain how the result changes. Check an empty or boundary case when the preconditions allow it.
